adventure.title: Ride the Boulder Creek Path End to End
adventure.description: Six car-free miles tracing the creek from the mouth of the canyon out to the plains — the spine of how Boulder actually gets around.
adventure.bonus: Stop at every underpass mural you pass.

adventure.title: Drive Flagstaff to Lost Gulch Overlook
adventure.description: Switchback up Flagstaff Mountain to a rock perch where the plains run flat to Kansas and the sunset does all the work.
adventure.bonus: Get there before the sun does and claim the best rock.

adventure.title: Paddleboard Boulder Reservoir at Golden Hour
adventure.description: Flat water, the whole Front Range skyline on one shore, and a board you can rent on the spot for an hour of easy balance work.
adventure.bonus: Make it from shore to shore without falling in.

adventure.title: Ski Your Backyard Mountain at Eldora
adventure.description: Twenty-one miles from Pearl Street — no I-70, no resort theatre, just Boulder County's own hill and a Woodward park to session.
adventure.bonus: Take one run through the terrain park even if you have no business there.

adventure.title: Hike to Blue Lake at Brainard
adventure.description: An hour from town and suddenly you're at eleven thousand feet beside a glacial lake with Mount Toll filling the whole skyline.
adventure.bonus: Put a hand in the water and hold it there for ten seconds.

adventure.title: Rip the Canyon Loop at Betasso Preserve
adventure.description: Flowy singletrack through ponderosa above Boulder Canyon — the ride locals do after work and still rave about.
adventure.bonus: Clear the whole loop without unclipping once.

adventure.title: Hike to Royal Arch
adventure.description: A short, savage climb out of Chautauqua that pays off at a natural sandstone arch framing the city below.
adventure.bonus: Sit under the arch until you can hear nothing but wind.

adventure.title: Guided Trad Climb in Eldorado Canyon
adventure.description: Rope up on the red sandstone walls that made American rock climbing, with a Colorado Mountain School guide handling the gear and the fear.
adventure.bonus: Lead the last pitch yourself, even if it's the easy one.

adventure.title: Float Boulder Creek on a Tube
adventure.description: Snowmelt straight off the Divide, a cheap tube, and a lazy mile of whitewater right through the middle of town.
adventure.bonus: Keep your sunglasses on for the whole run.

adventure.title: Sunrise Balloon Flight over Boulder Valley
adventure.description: Lift off before dawn and watch the Flatirons go from grey to burning orange from a thousand feet up, champagne waiting on landing.
adventure.bonus: Help pack the envelope away at the end — it's harder than it looks.

adventure.title: Walk the Mesa Trail End to End
adventure.description: Seven miles along the base of the Flatirons from Chautauqua to Eldorado Springs, with the whole rock wall rising beside you the entire way.
adventure.bonus: Finish at the Eldorado Springs end and soak your legs in the creek.

adventure.title: Scramble the First and Second Flatirons
adventure.description: Climb the slabs that put Boulder on every postcard, topping out on tilted sandstone with the whole Front Range laid out below you.
adventure.bonus: Touch the summit block of the Second before you touch your phone.

adventure.title: Learn to Lead in Boulder Canyon
adventure.description: A half-day of granite sport climbing fifteen minutes up the canyon, with a guide turning you from a gym climber into an outdoor one.
adventure.bonus: Climb one route in your approach shoes.

adventure.title: Loop Walker Ranch Above the Canyon
adventure.description: A brutal, beautiful 7.6-mile loop that drops to South Boulder Creek and makes you earn every foot back — the local trail-runner's benchmark.
adventure.bonus: Run the final climb out instead of walking it.

adventure.title: Catch Sunrise on Mount Sanitas
adventure.description: Boulder's lung-burning local favourite — a steep rock staircase that puts you on a ridgeline just as the plains light up.
adventure.bonus: Start in the dark. No headlamp, no excuses.

adventure.title: Project Night at Movement Boulder
adventure.description: Twenty-two thousand square feet of walls and a hundred-plus boulder problems in the town where half the climbing world trains.
adventure.bonus: Try the problem two grades above you until you fall off it five times.

social.title: Trivia Night at the Rayback
social.description: Thirty taps, a food truck lot and a room full of over-educated Boulderites who take bar trivia far too seriously.
social.bonus: Pick a team name that gets read out loud and lands.

social.title: Rooftop Round at Avanti
social.description: Two bars, a top deck over Pearl Street and six kitchens downstairs if anyone gets hungry — the easiest group plan in Boulder.
social.bonus: Everyone orders for the person on their left.

social.title: Sweaty Front Row at the Fox Theatre
social.description: Five hundred capacity on The Hill, consistently rated one of the best-sounding rooms in America — close enough to the stage to get stepped on.
social.bonus: Buy a ticket to a band you've never heard before tonight.

social.title: Living-Room Gig at Velvet Elk
social.description: Plush seating, odd taxidermy, dim lamps and a band three feet away — the smallest good room in Boulder.
social.bonus: Talk to the musician at the merch table afterwards.

social.title: Cocktails in the Catacombs at License No. 1
social.description: Down the stairs under the Hotel Boulderado into a brick cellar that held one of Colorado's first liquor licences — now a proper cocktail room with a jazz lounge.
social.bonus: Order a classic you can't pronounce and let them correct you.

social.title: Sit at the Bar at The Bitter Bar
social.description: A loungey back-alley room where the man often called Colorado's godfather of cocktails has been making the classics correctly for over a decade.
social.bonus: Tell the bartender one spirit and one mood, then hand it over.

social.title: Work Through the Taps at Avery
social.description: Thirty-plus beers from one of the loudest, hoppiest names in American craft, poured in a glass-and-steel taphouse east of town.
social.bonus: Order the highest-ABV thing on the board and respect it.

social.title: Tapas Hour on the Corrida Rooftop
social.description: Four storeys up with gin and tonics the size of fishbowls and the Flatirons going pink while you work through the pintxos list.
social.bonus: Be on the roof the moment the Flatirons turn red.

social.title: Buffs Gameday at Folsom Field
social.description: Fifty thousand people in a bowl at the foot of the Flatirons, Ralphie the live buffalo running the field, and The Hill absolutely feral afterwards.
social.bonus: Stay standing for Ralphie's run and the whole first quarter.

social.title: Stout Month at Mountain Sun
social.description: Every February this Pearl Street institution turns its entire board over to stouts — no reservations, cash-friendly, deliberately stuck in 1993.
social.bonus: Try four different stouts and rank them out loud.

social.title: Skee-Ball Tournament at Press Play
social.description: Old cabinets, pinball, skee-ball, giant Jenga and a DJ three nights a week — competitive nostalgia with a full bar attached.
social.bonus: Loser of the skee-ball final buys the next round.

social.title: Show Night at the Boulder Theater
social.description: A 1906 art-deco hall on 14th Street that takes everything from the Boulder Phil to Old Crow Medicine Show, under a painted ceiling.
social.bonus: Get there early enough to stand dead centre on the floor.

culture.title: Free Factory Tour at Celestial Seasonings
culture.description: Hairnet on, forty-five minutes through a working tea factory, and a Mint Room so potent it makes your eyes water — all of it free.
culture.bonus: Last a full thirty seconds inside the Mint Room.

culture.title: Dome Show at Fiske Planetarium
culture.description: One of the largest planetarium domes between Chicago and LA, running live sky talks and full-dome films on a campus full of actual space scientists.
culture.bonus: Stay for the Q&A and ask the one question you're embarrassed by.

culture.title: Double Bill at the Dairy Arts Center
culture.description: A converted dairy that now holds three theatres, a cinema and gallery space — Boulder's one-stop shop for everything not on Pearl Street.
culture.bonus: See the show you understand least.

culture.title: Shakespeare Under the Stars at the Mary Rippon
culture.description: Seventy years of outdoor Shakespeare in a stone amphitheatre on the CU campus, bats overhead and the Flatirons going dark behind the stage.
culture.bonus: Bring a blanket and stay for the curtain call applause.

culture.title: First Friday in the NoBo Art District
culture.description: North Broadway's warehouses and studios throw their doors open on the first Friday of the month — working artists, cheap wine, no velvet rope.
culture.bonus: Talk to an artist about their own work for five minutes.

culture.title: Current Shows at BMoCA
culture.description: A small, sharp contemporary museum on Canyon with rotating regional work and a programme far braver than its square footage.
culture.bonus: Pick the piece you'd hang at home and defend it.

culture.title: Fossils at the CU Museum of Natural History
culture.description: A free university collection heavy on Colorado paleontology — the dinosaurs that came out of the ground an hour from here.
culture.bonus: Find the oldest thing in the building.

culture.title: Colorado Music Festival at Chautauqua
culture.description: Six weeks of orchestral music every summer inside an 1898 wooden auditorium with the doors open and the Flatirons right outside them.
culture.bonus: Sit in the cheap seats at the back where the wood resonates.

chill.title: Brewery Tour at Upslope's Lee Hill
chill.description: The original North Boulder brewhouse where Upslope still runs its experiments — a short tour, then the odd stuff on tap.
chill.bonus: Drink whichever experimental batch they're least sure about.

chill.title: Patio Afternoon at Sanitas Brewing
chill.description: The biggest brewery patio in Boulder, with a taco kitchen, a view toward the mountain it's named for, and nowhere else to be.
chill.bonus: Stay for a second round you didn't plan on.

chill.title: Pour-Over at Ozo on Pearl
chill.description: Boulder's own roaster since 2009, pulling careful shots in a small room where everyone seems to have just come down off something.
chill.bonus: Ask what the single origin is and actually taste for it.

chill.title: Busker Roulette on Pearl Street Mall
chill.description: Four car-free blocks of street performers, zip-line bike kids and chalk artists — Boulder's living room, free of charge.
chill.bonus: Tip the strangest act you find.

chill.title: Sunset on the Chautauqua Lawn
chill.description: A sloping green at the foot of the Flatirons with a 19th-century auditorium behind you — the best free seat in Boulder.
chill.bonus: Stay through full dark and find one satellite.

chill.title: Walk the Mesa at NCAR
chill.description: I.M. Pei designed the research lab to echo the Flatirons behind it; the short trail out front is one of the quietest views in town.
chill.bonus: Read every interpretive sign on the Walter Orr Roberts trail.

chill.title: Lose an Hour in Boulder Book Store
chill.description: Three floors of creaking independent bookshop on Pearl Street, with over two hundred author events a year and staff picks worth trusting.
chill.bonus: Buy whatever book the staff-pick shelf argues hardest for.

chill.title: Swim the Artesian Pool at Eldorado Springs
chill.description: A 1900s spring-fed pool at the mouth of Eldorado Canyon, cold enough to shock you awake with sandstone walls rising on every side.
chill.bonus: Get all the way under on the first attempt.

chill.title: Chai and Used Paperbacks at Trident
chill.description: Employee-owned since 1980 — a cramped, perfect bookshop-café where Boulder goes to read alone in company.
chill.bonus: Stay until you finish a whole chapter without checking your phone.

chill.title: Afternoon Tea at the Dushanbe Teahouse
chill.description: Hand-carved in Tajikistan, crated across the world and rebuilt beside Boulder Creek as a gift from a sister city — then filled with tea.
chill.bonus: Pick a tea purely by the name on the menu.

foodie.title: Wood-Fired Napoletana at Pizzeria Alberico
foodie.description: The Frasca team's pizza room next door to the flagship — blistered Neapolitan pies out of a wood oven, at a fraction of the fine-dining bill.
foodie.bonus: Eat one pie with your hands, folded, standing at the bar.

foodie.title: Oysters and a Martini at Jax Fish House
foodie.description: Thirty years of flying in shellfish to a landlocked mountain town, shucked at a loud bar in the middle of Pearl Street.
foodie.bonus: Try a variety you've never heard of and guess the coast.

foodie.title: The Friuli Tasting Menu at Frasca
foodie.description: A Michelin star and a James Beard Outstanding Restaurant award for one narrow idea done perfectly: the food and wine of northeastern Italy, in a strip-mall-adjacent room on Pearl.
foodie.bonus: Let the sommelier pick every pour — no questions, no vetoes.

foodie.title: Ugly Crust Pizza at The Sink
foodie.description: A century of CU students have signed these walls and low ceilings — Obama ate here, Redford mopped the floors, and the pizza is deliberately misshapen.
foodie.bonus: Find your own signature on the wall, or leave one where nobody will look.

foodie.title: Stall Crawl at Avanti Boulder
foodie.description: Six kitchens, two bars and a rooftop deck in the old Cheesecake Factory shell — arepas, Taiwanese, deli and pizza without anybody having to compromise.
foodie.bonus: Order one thing from every stall and share the lot.

foodie.title: Build a Picnic Basket at Cured
foodie.description: Eighty rotating cheeses, salumi off Frasca's old slicer, cheap good wine and a wicker basket — assembled for a hillside twenty minutes away.
foodie.bonus: Let the counter pick all three cheeses for you.

foodie.title: Whole-Animal Dinner at Blackbelly
foodie.description: Top Chef winner Hosea Rosenberg's butcher shop and restaurant under one roof, where the cut on your plate was broken down forty feet away.
foodie.bonus: Order the thing on the menu you can't identify.

foodie.title: Dinner at Oak at Fourteenth
foodie.description: Wood-fired New American from a Frasca alum, in a room they rebuilt from the studs up after a fire took the original.
foodie.bonus: Start with whatever came off the oak grill today, no substitutions.

foodie.title: Basque Steak and Gin Tonics at Corrida
foodie.description: Spanish fire-cooking on a fourth-floor rooftop, with the Flatirons close enough to feel and a txuleta built for two.
foodie.bonus: Split the biggest steak on the menu and finish it.

foodie.title: Breakfast Burrito at Santo
foodie.description: Northern New Mexican cooking from a chef who grew up in Taos — roasted chile that actually tastes like somewhere, wrapped to go.
foodie.bonus: Order it Christmas — red and green — and pick a side by the last bite.

foodie.title: Food Truck Roulette at the Rayback
foodie.description: Four trucks that rotate twice a day, a thirty-tap bar and a huge lawn — Boulder's default answer to 'where should we go?'
foodie.bonus: Eat from whichever truck has the shortest line, sight unseen.

foodie.title: Saturday Morning at the Boulder Farmers Market
foodie.description: Forty years of Front Range growers lining 13th Street — breakfast from the vendors, live music, and the whole town out in running clothes.
foodie.bonus: Buy something you've never cooked and figure it out tonight.

8ball.title: Pearl Street Roulette
8ball.description: Wildcard: walk the length of the Pearl Street Mall and let the first busker you stop for choose your night — their favourite bar, their favourite taco, their call.
8ball.bonus: Actually go where they send you, no matter how strange.

8ball.title: Above the City Before Breakfast
8ball.description: Wildcard: pick any trailhead at Chautauqua, start in the dark, and be standing higher than every building in Boulder when the sun clears the plains.
8ball.bonus: Eat breakfast still covered in trail dust.
